title: Quantum Sample
text: Quantum mechanics is a fundamental theory in physics that describes the behavior of nature at and below the scale of atoms. Superposition is a fundamental principle of quantum mechanics. It states that a physical system exists partly in all its particular theoretically possible states simultaneously. Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon that occurs when a group of particles are generated, interact, or share spatial proximity in such a way that the quantum state of each particle cannot be described independently of the state of the others. The Heisenberg uncertainty principle is a fundamental limit to the precision with which certain pairs of physical properties can be simultaneously known.

title: Retrieval Sample
text: Retrieval augmented generation systems first retrieve relevant context and then ask a language model to answer using that context. Chunking controls how source documents are split before indexing. Smaller chunks can improve precision, while larger chunks can preserve more context. Embedding models convert text into vectors so that semantically related passages can be compared by similarity. Benchmarking retrieval strategies requires fixed questions, known answer sentences, and repeatable metrics.
